anya (ml-eng): Heads up — enabled FP8 hybrid-GEMM kernels on H100 + L40S for redwood-v2-base canary. Quick eval shows small generation-quality drift at long contexts (4096+) and intermittent activation "overflow" signs in the logs. Anyone seen this?

mike (runtime): hmm. Can you paste the runtime flags and a tiny repro?

anya (ml-eng): repro bits below. Baseline is `fp16` with our usual kv-cache flow. Repro:```
model=redwood-v2-base
seq_len=4096
batch=1
quant_mode=fp8_hybrid
runtime_flags=--enable-fp8 --fp8-policy=hybrid-gemm --fp8-autoscale=auto
```
Observed: short-context (<=512) matches baseline. For seq>=2048 we see PPL jump ~6-8% and occasional `activation_scale=NaN` lines in the node logs.

lisa (ml-infra): do you have kernel version & cuobjdump? L40S tiling sometimes differs from H100, leads to different reduction ordering. Could be accumulation rounding + autoscale interplay.

anya (ml-eng): kernel sha: `rev-2026-07-g7a9b`. Using driver 535.xx on H100 and 540.xx on L40S. Logs:```
[2026-03-20 17:22:10] kernel_xmma.cu: matmul_reduce: exponent overflow at i=1024
[2026-03-20 17:22:10] runtime: activation_scale NaN, fallback to fp16 cache
```

ryan (research): this rings a bell — FP8 autoscaling heuristics (per-tile vs per-block) can diverge when the tiling changes. If L40S uses a different tile width the per-GEMM max can spike and push the scale exponent too high. In our AWQ/GPTQ tests we saw similar micro-regressions but lower freq.

mike (runtime): try forcing `--fp8-autoscale=per-layer` or `--fp8-autoscale=clamp` to see if it stabilizes. Also try `--fp8-clamp-exp=6` as a quick hotpatch.

anya (ml-eng): tried `per-layer` — PPL improved (delta down to ~1.5%) and logs stopped showing NaN, but throughput dropped ~3%. Will run full eval.

lisa (ml-infra): another angle: KV-cache layout. If the runtime switches to a different kernel for long KV (tiling change) the mixed-precision path may not have the same post-processing clamp we expect. Can you dump which matmul kernel is used (set `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_select`)?

anya (ml-eng): good idea. Dump shows: for seq<=1024 we use `gemm_sm90_alpha`, for seq>=2048 we use `gemm_sm90_tiled_v2`.

ryan (research): exactly — `tiled_v2` doesn't yet have the more conservative exponent clamp. That explains both the NaN and the PPL blip. We should either backport the clamp or add a fallback to fp16 for that kernel.

sofia (eng-ml): action items: 1) mike — add `fp8-clamp-exp` knob to tiled_v2 kernel asap (short PR). 2) lisa — run canary on L40S with `--fp8-autoscale=per-layer` to measure throughput/quality tradeoff. 3) anya — run the long-context eval suite (4096, 8192) on both H100 & L40S and post diffs. I'll coordinate rollout windows.

mike (runtime): acked. Small patch ready, will push canary build `rev-2026-07-g7a9b-1` with clamp default `exp<=6`.

deploy-bot: started canary deploy of `runtime/rev-2026-07-g7a9b-1` to dedicated-l40s-qa :rocket:

anya (ml-eng): quick note — please include a test that runs deterministic seeds for sampling; FP8 can change randomness in softmax numerics and make evaluation flaky. Seeded-generation tests added to my eval harness.

ryan (research): also add a small synthetic with extreme activation ranges (scaled inputs) to validate clamp boundary. We caught this earlier in lab but not in canary.

sofia (eng-ml): timeline: mike patch in canary now, lisa to run 12h canary tests, if stable we roll to dedicated-l40s-prod next Tuesday. If regressions persist we'll fallback that kernel to fp16 for long-kv path.

anya (ml-eng): thanks. I'll post the eval table once runs complete. :eyes:

mike (runtime): FYI, putting a short-term doc in `docs/quant/notes.md` about per-kernel autoscale gotchas. :memo: 

ryan (research): nice. Long-term we should add per-tiling evals to our model onboarding checklist so FP8 bakeoffs include tile-variation sweeps.

sofia (eng-ml): agreed. assign to onboarding checklist item. closing for now unless anyone has other hot findings. :thumbsup:
